gastronomy:Varvakios Central Market.name: Varvakios Central Market
gastronomy:Varvakios Central Market.teaser: Shaved ice, sardine silver and auction voices under the iron roof the Varvakis bequest paid for
gastronomy:Varvakios Central Market.story: Ioannis Varvakis left Psara as a sailor and made his fortune in Caspian caviar; his bequest paid for the school and the covered market that carry his name, built between 1876 and 1886 on Athinas. Come at first light, when the fish hall is a theatre: crates tipped onto shaved ice, drifts of sardines and gavros, red mullet laid out in rows, and the stallholders calling prices across the aisles under the iron arches. Through the side door the meat hall hangs its carcasses, and across Athinas the fruit and vegetable stalls fill the opposite block. Floors are wet and cash still settles most sales.
gastronomy:Varvakios Central Market.why: Go before eight, when the morning's catch is still being laid out and the chefs are buying.
facts: From dawn into the afternoon; listings disagree on the exact closing (08:00–18:00 seen Jul 2026, 06:00–16:00 in a May 2026 directory)
Early morning, for the fish hall at full voice
Small-boat sardines, gavros and barbounia in summer, when the trawl ban leaves deep-water fish off the ice; closed shoes for the wet floor

gastronomy:Kallidromiou Saturday Laiki.name: Kallidromiou Saturday Laiki
gastronomy:Kallidromiou Saturday Laiki.teaser: One graffiti-walled Exarcheia street of Attica growers, from Marathon lettuces to Megara eggs
gastronomy:Kallidromiou Saturday Laiki.story: Every Saturday Kallidromiou, the street that climbs under Strefi Hill, turns into a farmers' row. Attica smallholders stack Marathon lettuces, Megara eggs and whatever the week has ripened against walls thick with graffiti, and the regulars know the sellers by name: the egg man Angelos Koursos, and Vasilis Makoudakis, half a century at his stall. A café on the street opens at 05:30 for the stallholders before the shoppers arrive. Prices are by the kilo and set by the growers, and the produce is strictly what is in season this week, nothing flown in.
gastronomy:Kallidromiou Saturday Laiki.why: Shop it like a chef: come early for choice, or after 13:30 when the last-hour prices drop.
facts: Early for the pick; after 13:30 for the bargains
Megara eggs, Marathon greens, seasonal fruit by the kilo; bring cash and your own bags

gastronomy:Mokka Specialty Coffee.name: Mokka
gastronomy:Mokka Specialty Coffee.teaser: A century of roasting at Athinas 44, opposite the market: buy the beans the city's cafés brew
gastronomy:Mokka Specialty Coffee.story: Mokka has roasted and ground coffee at Athinas 44, facing the Varvakios block, since 1923, and the smell reaches the pavement before the door does. Nikos Psomas runs it in the fourth generation; the house is a member of the Alliance for Coffee Excellence, the body behind the Cup of Excellence auctions, and it now supplies roasted coffee to more than five hundred businesses. The old shop counter still grinds to order for a briki, a filter or an espresso machine, and the specialty lots sit beside the Greek blends. How to drink the hot-sand coffee is told with the drinks; this card is for the bag you carry out.
gastronomy:Mokka Specialty Coffee.why: Tell them how the galley brews and they will grind to match; it keeps the boat's coffee honest for weeks.

gastronomy:Mastihashop.name: Mastihashop
gastronomy:Mastihashop.teaser: The Chios mastic growers' own counter in Athens: PDO resin, from raw tears to liqueur
gastronomy:Mastihashop.story: Only the mastic villages of southern Chios can make the lentisk tree weep its resin in commercial quantity, and UNESCO inscribed that know-how on its intangible heritage list in 2014. The growers' association, founded in 1938, opened mastihashop in 2002 to sell the PDO resin under its own name, with the profits returning to the villages. On the Panepistimiou corner the raw tears come in small tins: they crack like pine-scented glass between the teeth, then soften into a chew with a church-incense perfume. Beside them stand the liqueur, the sweets and the cooking powder.
gastronomy:Mastihashop.why: Buy the raw tears for the pastry section: a pinch of ground mastiha changes a custard or an ice cream.
facts: Panepistimiou 6, corner of Kriezotou, near Syntagma
Monday to Saturday; closed Sunday (seen Jul 2026; check before going)

gastronomy:Bahar.name: Bahar
gastronomy:Bahar.teaser: Since 1940 the doorway that makes Evripidou smell of Evripidou: 2,500 jars, weighed to order
gastronomy:Bahar.story: Antonis Manolessos came to Athens from Santorini and opened at Evripidou 31, a step from the Varvakios, in 1940, months before Greece went to war; his son Matthaios has kept the counter since 1976. The shelves run to more than 2,500 references, from spices and herbs to mineral salts, dried vegetables, rare roots and special flours. Krokos Kozanis saffron, wild oregano on the branch and mountain tea are weighed into paper bags on the old scales while the queue waits on the pavement. This Is Athens counts it among the addresses local chefs and food writers swear by.
gastronomy:Bahar.why: Arrive with a written list: the range is too deep to browse when the queue is out the door.
facts: Monday to Saturday; closed Sunday (seen Jul 2026)

gastronomy:Aristokratikon.name: Aristokratikon
gastronomy:Aristokratikon.teaser: Whole Aegina pistachios sealed in dark chocolate by the city's oldest chocolatier, a step off Syntagma
gastronomy:Aristokratikon.story: Panagiotis Karras came down from Epirus and opened in 1928, and his descendants still make everything by hand. Maria Callas and Jackie Onassis were customers, but the counter's best argument is Greek: whole Aegina pistachios bound in dark chocolate, Skopelos prunes, Pelion chestnuts glazed and wrapped, loukoumia by the box. The city shop is now at Voulis 7, a short walk from Syntagma, small and glass-fronted, with the pralines laid out like jewellery. Chocolate suffers in an Athens August, so this is a cool-month errand, or one for the last stop before the tender.
gastronomy:Aristokratikon.why: Take the pistachio clusters back as the guest gift; they are the one thing here no other shop copies.
facts: Monday to Saturday; closed Sunday (seen Jul 2026)

around:Domaine Papagiannakos.name: Domaine Papagiannakos
around:Domaine Papagiannakos.teaser: Old-vine Savatiano and a modern retsina, poured in Greece's first bioclimatic winery on the Mesogeia plain
around:Domaine Papagiannakos.story: The Mesogeia plain east of Athens was the ancient city's vineyard, and Savatiano its workhorse grape, long blamed for bad retsina. The Papagiannakos family, bottling since 1919, set out to prove the grape wrong. In 2007 Vassilis Papagiannakos opened a gravity-fed winery outside Markopoulo that the family describes as the first bioclimatic winery in Greece, and from 50 to 60 year old dry-farmed vines he makes Savatiano with baked apple, fresh almond and a thyme-scrub salinity. The Retsina of Mesogaia, resinated lightly, is the bottle that changed minds about Attica's own wine.
around:Domaine Papagiannakos.why: Book the tasting and taste the Savatiano and the retsina side by side; that pair is the whole argument.
facts: By car or taxi to Markopoulo Mesogaias, about 35 km east of central Athens; about half an hour from the Riviera

around:Cape Sounion.name: Cape Sounion
around:Cape Sounion.teaser: White Doric columns on the last headland of Attica, where Byron cut his name and the day ends over the sea
around:Cape Sounion.story: At the southern tip of Attica the Temple of Poseidon stands on a cliff above the Aegean, built around 444 to 440 BC, in the same years and the same classical manner as the Parthenon. What survives is a row of white marble Doric columns that turn gold, then pink, as the sun drops into the sea to the west. Lord Byron came in 1810 and carved his name into the stone; you cannot walk inside the temple now, so look for it from the rope. He put the cape in The Isles of Greece: 'Place me on Sunium's marbled steep.'
around:Cape Sounion.why: Time it for the last hour of light, and take the coast road there: the drive down the Riviera is half the outing.
facts: KTEL Attikis bus from Pedion Areos (Alexandras Avenue) along the coast road, about 2 hours; by car or taxi down the Athens Riviera

around:The islands are another guide.name: The islands are another guide
around:The islands are another guide.teaser: Aegina, its PDO pistachio and the growers' co-op now live in the Piraeus & Saronic guide
around:The islands are another guide.story: The Saronic islands used to sit in this guide; they now have their own, with the harbour and Piraeus. That includes Aegina, where pistachios took to the dry volcanic soil better than anywhere in Greece and where Fistiki Aeginis has been a protected designation of origin since 1996. The growers' co-op, founded in 1947, sells the real thing on the harbourfront. Anywhere else, read the label: 'Aegina-style' on a bag means nothing.
around:The islands are another guide.why: For the nuts, the co-op and the ferry, open the Piraeus & Saronic guide at /terroir/Piraeus-Saronic/.

follow:Athens Epidaurus Festival.name: Athens Epidaurus Festival
follow:Athens Epidaurus Festival.teaser: With the Herodeon closed for restoration, the festival plays Peiraios 260 and the theatre at Epidaurus
follow:Athens Epidaurus Festival.story: For decades the Athens summer meant a concert in the Odeon of Herodes Atticus, under the Acropolis slope. That ended, for now, with the farewell programme of 3 to 30 June 2026: the Roman theatre is closed for at least three years while its arched facade and marble seating are stabilised and two ancient mosaics are uncovered. Iefimerida reported a planned reopening in early 2029; the culture minister, Lina Mendoni, has said only that it will need at least three years. Meanwhile the festival carries on at Peiraios 260 in the city and at the Ancient Theatre of Epidaurus in the Peloponnese.
follow:Athens Epidaurus Festival.why: Check the bill before promising guests a night at an ancient theatre: in Athens itself there is none until the Herodeon reopens.

follow:The MICHELIN Guide, Greece.name: The MICHELIN Guide, Greece
follow:The MICHELIN Guide, Greece.teaser: The live Greek selection, about to widen from Athens to Thessaloniki and Santorini
follow:The MICHELIN Guide, Greece.story: MICHELIN first rated Athens on its own, and Delta, in the Stavros Niarchos Foundation Cultural Center, took two stars and a Green Star at its first evaluation in the 2022 guide, then kept both stars in 2024. There was no new Athens selection in 2025. In December 2025 MICHELIN announced that Thessaloniki and Santorini would join Athens, with the first three-city selection due in the second half of 2026; Greek City Times reported on 9 October 2026 that it would be unveiled on 20 October, labelled the 2027 selection. Stars move every edition, so read the live list, not last year's.
follow:The MICHELIN Guide, Greece.why: Check the site the week you book: the new Greek list lands in late October 2026.

follow:laikesagores.gr.name: laikesagores.gr
follow:laikesagores.gr.teaser: The laiki listings: which open-air market fills which street on which day
follow:laikesagores.gr.story: Athens shops for produce at the laiki, the open-air street market that sets up in a different neighbourhood each day from Monday to Saturday, closing on public holidays. The markets are run under the Attica Region, which moves or suspends them by official notice, for roadworks, a storm or a holiday. laikesagores.gr lists the markets by street and day, and that is the page to check before planning a provisioning run around one; the Kallidromiou Saturday market has its own card.
follow:laikesagores.gr.why: Check it before a holiday weekend, when markets move days or close.

follow:Athinorama.name: Athinorama
follow:Athinorama.teaser: The city's listings magazine, and the list that tells you who stays open in August
follow:Athinorama.story: Athinorama is where Athenians look up what is on: theatre, cinema, music and restaurants, with its own critics' reviews. For a crew it earns its place once a year. Around 15 August, Dekapentavgoustos, the city empties; family tavernas, bakeries and small shops close for one to three weeks, and opening hours online go stale. Athinorama publishes a current-year list of restaurants open through August, and that list, checked against a phone call, is how you keep a summer table booking honest.
follow:Athinorama.why: In July, read its 'open in August' list before you book anything for the middle of the month.
facts: Athens listings and restaurant reviews, with an annual 'open in August' list
